# NSPanel HAUI 0.5.2

0.5.2 fixes four schedule problems, adds the dashboard card and six colorful predefined themes, and reorganizes the editor: Fleet and the device screen, the device settings behind a tile grid, and separate **Backups**, **Updates** and **Themes** sidebars. It updates the integration and the editor; the firmware only carries the new version number and both TFTs are unchanged, so the release keeps requiring display version 0.4.5.

## Before updating

Loading the panel store changes two stored settings and logs a warning for each:

- A schedule entry with its own dimmed brightness now needs the device's **Brightness dimmed**. Devices without one get 20 % (the panel's default); check it under **Screen** in the device settings ([upgrade notes](docs/user/update.md#a-schedule-entry-that-dims-needs-a-dimmed-brightness)).
- `theme_variant` is dropped from every device's settings. A theme now picks its own icon palette, so a light theme switches to the light-background icons on its own; remove `theme_variant` from hand-written YAML ([upgrade notes](docs/user/update.md#the-theme-picks-its-own-icon-colors)).

Nothing else needs a step: no TFT update, and no firmware change beyond the version number.

## Breaking changes

- **The theme picks its own icon colors.** The **Theme variant** switch is gone and the Theme sidebar no longer asks which palette to edit. A dark theme draws the dark-background weather, alarm and climate icons, a light theme such as **Light**, **White** or **Sky** the light-background ones; a theme can no longer pair its page with the other contrast.
- **A schedule entry that dims needs a dimmed brightness.** The device's **Brightness dimmed** is the brightness outside an entry and is now required when an entry sets its own. Before, a device could leave it empty, the hub had nothing to restore, and the panel kept the entry's brightness after it ended. Giving an entry a dimmed brightness while the device has none takes the panel's **Brightness Dimmed** reading (20 % when it reports none), says so, and saves it with the settings; a hand-written configuration that sets one without the other is refused when it is saved.

## Added

- **Dashboard card** — `custom:nspanel-haui-card` puts a device's home panel or its live screen on any dashboard, view-only, for every signed-in user and without admin rights ([Dashboard Card](docs/user/dashboard-card.md)).
- **Predefined themes** — **Midnight**, **Ocean**, **Forest**, **Sunset**, **Violet** and the light **Sky** beside the neutral **Dark**, **Light**, **White** and **Black**. Each sets every semantic page color, and its own background picks the matching icon palette ([Themes](docs/user/configuration/themes.md)).
- **Device settings groups** — the settings open on a grid of tiles, one per group (**General**, **Screen**, **Sounds**, **Home & idle**, **Gestures**, **Screen buttons**, **Hardware buttons**, **Advanced**), each naming what it holds. A tile opens the group's page, the sidebar strip's back arrow returns to the grid, and **Save** and **Cancel** in the footer apply the whole device as one draft ([Device Settings](docs/user/configuration/device.md#device-settings)).
- **Schedule in the device settings** — the **Schedule** group sits at the end of **Screen**, below the brightness, dimming and display-off fields its entries fill from, so the values an entry inherits are shown once as those fields. **Schedule** and **Gestures** are groups now instead of sidebars, and the device's theme choice sits in **General** ([Schedule](docs/user/configuration/device.md#schedule), [Gestures](docs/user/configuration/device.md#gestures)).
- **Selecting a device on Fleet** — select a **Device inventory** row outside its name and buttons (or press Enter or Space on it) or the name strip under a card. Row and card highlight together, a row scrolls the cards to it, the selected card stays centered when you return from it, and selecting again clears it; the card's screen still opens the device.
- **Move to another device** — **Move to…** in a panel's **More** menu lists the hub's other devices. Moving keeps the panel's key unless the target device uses it, and the confirmation names the free key it got instead; settings of the old device that name the panel keep the key, as after **Delete**. ArrowRight opens the submenu, ArrowLeft returns to the menu ([The Panel List](docs/user/configuration/README.md#the-panel-list)).
- **Per-state values** — an item's name, icon, color and value, and a grid tile's colors, switch between **One value** and **Per state**: one row per entity state, suggested by the state field, instead of typed JSON. A state without a row keeps the default, and switching back keeps the current state's value ([Values that depend on the state](docs/user/configuration/items.md#values-that-depend-on-the-state)).
- **Latest events reset** — the timeline's second line names the device it is scoped to and closes with the window it covers (**Last 24 hours**, or **Since 14:32** after a reset); **Reset** on the title line restarts the list at the moment you press it, and **Last 24 hours** goes back ([Logs](docs/user/configuration/README.md#logs)).
- **Device inventory footer** — the inventory closes with one connection segment per device in its connection tone, so a full fleet's state reads at a glance.

## Changed

- **Entity names** — the entity picker, item lists, **Diagnostics** and the preview's entity tooltip show the entity's own name (*Lampa Kuchnia*) instead of Home Assistant's full name with the device in front (*NSPanel Salon Lampa Kuchnia*); the picker still finds an entity by its full name.
- **Device settings** — one field per row, with the **Home panel** and **Idle panels** pickers at the right edge like the switches; **Screen** lists the brightness values and timeouts first, then the auto dimming and auto display-off switches and the schedule.
- **Backups, Updates and Themes** — each opens a sidebar of its own from a full-width button below the **Connection** and **Diagnostics** cards; **Updates** and **Themes** name what they hold on their trailing edge, and **Themes** replaces **Edit theme**. The **Connection** card (formerly **Connection & device**) keeps only the readings.
- **Import and Export** — the **Backup** card is gone; its buttons moved into a **Backups** sidebar with one card per direction, **Import** naming what it replaces and that there is no undo ([Backups](docs/user/configuration/README.md#backups)).
- **Switches and type** — every switch sits at the right end of its row, after its label, and the editor uses one type scale at Home Assistant's sizes (title bar and page titles 20px, sidebar titles 18px, card titles 16px, names and values 14px, hints 13px), following the Home Assistant font size setting.
- **Update settings** — the **Update channel** is a list, and **Install firmware updates automatically** is a switch that replaces **When a new version is found**; the stored setting (`firmware_auto_update`) is unchanged.
- **Updates sidebar** — an offered firmware or display update is one badge from the installed to the new version (`0.5.2 → 0.5.3`), the integration's version moved to the end of the **Check for updates** row, and a narrow sidebar shortens the labels.
- **Fleet** — the dashboard fills a wide window, a long **Device inventory** scrolls under its column headings, **Latest events** takes the inventory's height, the carousel fades its right edge and dashed outlines fill the leftover width. **Latest events** lists only the last 24 hours' warnings and errors; a selected device scopes it and **Logs**, which holds the full log.
- **Device screen** — the **Connection** and **Diagnostics** tiles use smaller values, with the Wi-Fi bars at the tile's edge; the Wi-Fi strength stays visible while the panel is offline, the dot keeps the connection state, and the uptime tile is green while the panel is online and stable.
- **Integration, not hub** — Fleet and **Diagnostics** say **Integration version**, **Integration log** and **Integration details**, as the Updates sidebar and the panel's About page already did.
- **Panel overview** — the **Home panel** and **Idle panel** tiles show the role's icon beside the role and panel, and stack on a narrow card.
- **Panel count** — group headings say **Navigation (1 panel)** instead of **Navigation (1 panels)**.

## Fixed

### Schedule

- **Dimmed brightness after an entry** — it no longer stays after the entry ends; see *Breaking changes*.
- **Auto display off** — saving the settings with a changed switch while an entry was active wrote the panel's switch a second time and could override the entry. While the schedule has entries it owns the switch alone; removing every entry sets it once from **Auto display off**, after which automations control it again.
- **Daylight saving time** — the time to the next entry was counted on the wall clock, so an entry could start an hour early or late on the day the clocks change; it now starts on time.
- **Polar night** — where the sun did not rise or set until the next day, the hub stopped looking for the next sunrise or sunset entry until the panel reconnected; it now looks again every day.

### Editor

- **Home Assistant app** — the strip under the phone's status bar showed the page background above the title bar; the editor now handles the screen insets itself.
- **Entity hover** — with **Show entities in the preview** on, a Row panel's buttons, switch and slider name their entity too, a hardware button names the entity it switches (its relay in relay mode), the Live preview names the entity under the mouse (it raised an error on every mouse move before), and a widget whose entity Home Assistant does not have is named with a note that it is not found or unavailable.
- **Accessibility** — the dashboard meets WCAG AA contrast for status text, badges, icons and the primary button in light and dark themes, and a screen reader hears event levels, the page heading, named device cards and table columns, and rollout changes. An icon in a tone keeps the tone itself instead of the darker shade text needs.
- **Latest events** — the level dots carry their tone itself (a lighter blue, amber and red) instead of the dark text tone, which read almost black at 12px.
- **Fact tiles** — a tile keeps a long label or reading inside its border: the label wraps and the value moves to its own line, ellipsized only when it alone is too wide.

### Updates

- **Translations** — the reasons a firmware update is withheld or refused (differing build variants, no or an invalid firmware version, no build variant in the manifest) and the panel's installing notice are translated into every device language.
- **Unreadable manifest** — a manifest the hub could not read, or no check since Home Assistant started, reads as the reason nothing is offered instead of **Up to date**, and **Check for updates** shows an error from the release list.
- **Offline panel** — an offline panel, or a status the editor could not refresh, offers no **Install**, and the device screen and the Updates sidebar say the values are the last ones read.
- **Failed install** — a failed install clears once the panel reconnects with another firmware, and a second install while one runs is refused instead of reported as started.
- **Rollouts** — the dashboard notices a rollout another editor started, a finished rollout can be dismissed, and a rollout no longer waits on a device that was disabled or reloaded meanwhile.

### Integration

- **Device names** — the Home Assistant device that holds a panel's notify and update entities is named after the panel instead of "NSPanel HAUI Hub".
